issues.failure_explanation: On the compact torus, a periodic $C^2$ function cannot have $\nabla^2V\succeq\alpha I$ with $\alpha>0$: taking traces gives $\Delta V\ge d\alpha>0$, but the integral of $\Delta V$ over the torus is zero. Thus the stated sufficient condition is impossible.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace by a valid torus-compatible convexity condition or remove the claim.
issues.overall_effect: The background claim that displacement convexity follows from this condition is vacuous/misleading; no formal result later relies on this specific condition.
issues.title: Impossible convexity hypothesis on torus
issues.why_classification: It is a background sufficient condition, not used in the main proofs, and can be fixed locally.

issues.failure_explanation: A variational solution lies in $H^1(0,T;(H^1)^*)$, so its initial value must be in $(H^1)^*$. The space $L^1_+$ is not contained in $(H^1)^*$ in general, so for arbitrary $\mu_0\in L^1_+$ the condition $\mu(0)=\mu_0$ is not meaningful in the stated solution space.

failure_location.quote: Under the above assumptions on $V,W,\sigma$ and any $\mu_0\in L^1_+(\Omega)$, there exists a unique variational solution $\mu(t)$ of \eqref{eq:mckean_vlasov_repeat}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume $\mu_0\in L^1_+\cap(H^1)^*$ or use a weaker solution concept for general $L^1_+$ data.
issues.overall_effect: The global well-posedness theorem is not well-posed for the advertised class of all $L^1_+$ initial data, and later convergence statements using such initial data are affected.
issues.title: Initial data outside variational solution space
issues.why_classification: Restricting the initial data or changing the solution concept materially limits the stated scope, though it does not require new global architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: If $\mu_0$ vanishes on a set of positive measure, then $\mu(0,x)=0$ there, contradicting strict positivity for all $t\ge0$. The parabolic smoothing only gives strict positivity for $t>0$ (and typically a.e.).

failure_location.quote: for all times $t \ge 0$, $\int_{\Omega} \mu(t,x) \, dx =1$ and $\mu(t,x)>0$ for all $x \in \Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the conclusion for $t>0$ (and a.e. $x$), or assume $\mu_0>0$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the boundary time $t=0$ is affected; the positivity statement should exclude $t=0$ or assume a strictly positive initial density.
issues.title: Strict positivity claimed at time zero
issues.why_classification: A local degenerate-case correction preserves all substantive content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Combining Lemmas~\ref{lem:perturb-pure} and ~\ref{lem:K-bounded} concludes the result.
If $W \in W^{2,\infty}(\Omega)$, then $\K$ is Hilbert-Schmidt, hence compact, on $L^2(\Omega)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited lemmas show only that $\Hcal=\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}+\K$ is a compact perturbation of a self-adjoint operator, giving compact resolvent. They do not show $\K$ is self-adjoint or that $\Hcal$ is self-adjoint. A compact perturbation of a self-adjoint operator need not have real spectrum, and the kernel formula for $\K$ is not symmetric in general.

issues.title: Realness of spectrum not established for compact perturbation
issues.why_classification: It is a spectral claim with a missing nontrivial argument, though the main stabilization proof uses only discreteness and compactness.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By \autoref{lem:spectrum_finite}, the spectrum of $\Lcal$ in the half-plane $\Re\lambda\ge -\delta$ consists of exactly $m < \infty$ eigenvalues $\{\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\}$.

For any $\delta>0$, the set
  \[
  \bigl\{\lambda\in\sigma(\Lcal) : \Re(\lambda) \ge -\delta\bigr\}
  \]

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma only says the unstable set is finite. The theorem statement allows the first $m$ eigenpairs to satisfy the condition without asserting that there are no additional eigenvalues in the same half-plane. If more than $m$ such eigenvalues exist, the $m$ controls cannot make the Hautus test hold for all of them.

issues.title: Hautus theorem assumes m controls but does not require m to cover all unstable modes
issues.why_classification: The method survives, but the number of controls and the quantifier must be corrected; this is more than a local typo but not a complete loss of the approach.

issues.failure_explanation: Since $\W$ is quadratic, $\W(e^{-\delta t}z)=e^{-2\delta t}\W(z)$. In the $z$-equation one multiplies by $e^{\delta t}$, so the nonlinear term should be $e^{-\delta t}\W(z)$, not $e^{-2\delta t}\W(z)$. Thus the displayed transformed closed-loop equation has the wrong time-dependent nonlinear term.
issues.overall_effect: The closed-loop equation used for the contraction argument is not the exact equation obtained from the change of variables; the remainder estimates are for a different (smaller) nonlinearity.
issues.title: Wrong time scaling of the nonlinear remainder in the closed-loop equation
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and the same contraction estimates remain valid since both factors are bounded by one.

issues.failure_explanation: With $A=\lambda I-\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the sum $A+B$ equals $\lambda I-\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}-\delta I+\hat\B\hat\B^*\hat\Pi-\K$, which is not $\Hcal_{\Pi}=\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}+\K-\delta I+\hat\B\hat\B^*\hat\Pi$. The proof therefore does not apply maximal regularity to the intended operator $\Hcal_{\Pi}$.
